key_insight: Training LLMs can be viewed as transmitting information over a noisy channel: model size, data, and compute set the channel bandwidth and noise, producing a Shannon-style scaling law that explains both monotonic gains and observed non‑monotonic failures (e.g., catastrophic overtraining, quantization loss).
problem_solved: Existing monotonic power-law scaling laws cannot explain emergent non‑monotonic phenomena—situations where more compute or parameters worsen performance. This framework explains when and why performance degrades despite increased resources.
method: Map model parameters, data, and optimization to a noisy communication channel and interpret effective capacity using the Shannon–Hartley theorem.
Introduce noise terms (training noise, quantization noise, optimization error) into capacity formulas to derive a unified Shannon Scaling Law that predicts performance vs. compute and size.
Validate theory with empirical curves and use the capacity-based view to identify optimal compute/model regimes and thresholds where overtraining or quantization cause degradation.
impact: Provides a principled, predictive tool for choosing model size, compute budget, and quantization/regularization strategies, helping practitioners avoid counterintuitive performance drops and allocate resources more efficiently.
visual_elements: Schematic: LLM training as a noisy channel — encoder (data + model), noisy channel (optimization + quantization noise), decoder (task performance).
Curve plot: Performance vs. compute/model size showing classical monotonic power law vs. Shannon curve with non‑monotonic region and optimal peak.
Heatmap/phase diagram: Regions of safe scaling, overtraining, and quantization‑limited degradation as functions of model size and noise level.
Flowchart/cards: Practical decision rules (e.g., detect capacity limit, stop-training criterion, quantization risk checklist).
paper_title: LLMs as Noisy Channels: A Shannon Perspective on Model Capacity and Scaling Laws
paper_authors: Xu Ouyang, Deyi Liu, Yuhang Cai, Jing Liu, Yuan Yang
